reasons: Directionally correct and pro-Customer: the redline strikes the 'without reduction or termination rights' carve-out in Section 2.1 and subordinates the three-year take-or-pay minimum to Customer's termination rights, with pro-rata reduction — this removes the only obstacle to the 30-day convenience exit and preserves the already-compliant Section 9.4.

Deviation classification is defensible: Section 9.4 alone meets the preferred position, but an unqualified multi-year take-or-pay expressly disclaiming termination rights, with no order-of-precedence clause, is effectively the walk-away outcome (locked-in multi-year spend with no effective convenience exit). High severity is appropriate.

Failed check 'Customer convenience termination present' is a false negative here: the convenience right already exists in p0039, which is correctly left untouched; the edit is properly targeted at the conflicting commitment clause.

Changed-character ratio of 0.779 on p0012 is acceptable given the paragraph is a single short sentence — deleting the disclaimer alone would leave the annual minimum payable notwithstanding termination, so the added pro-rata reduction sentence is necessary to make the exit meaningful.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position (convenience exit without penalty in a multi-year term), and offers the three-months'-fees fallback.
